sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Musa acuminata is a large tropical herb and one ancestor of many cultivated bananas; botanically, it is not a tree. Its pseudostem is formed by leaf sheaths. The species is native to Southeast Asia and widely cultivated.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The very large leaves can reach about 2.7 m long and 60 cm wide and often tear in the wind. Purple bracts uncover rows of pale flowers. Wild forms produce fruits with hard seeds; many derived cultivated varieties are seedless.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: Cultivated bananas are eaten as fruit or vegetables depending on the variety. The illustration shows a seedless cultivated form and does not represent the typical fruits of wild forms.
